items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: But in that band was Brad Gowens

ctx.x: Hey, that's nice, Cliff; thank you very much. I tell you, we were gonna talk about Bobby Hackett. Now tell me something about your relationship with Bobby and when you first met him.

I first became acquainted with Bobby Hackett in 1934 and '5, possibly 1935, when I was with the Dan Murphy band back in Boston. And I used to go down to an after hours club which was called The Theatrical Club, in Boston -- and Bobby had a little jazz band; Bobby had been playing for only a little over a year on trumpet. He had been playing guitar for several years; he had been working with around Boston, a lot of club dates, I guess with society club dates on the guitar. He was from Providence, Rhode Island.

And for a fast resume, he worked at the Theatrical Club, as I say, and it might be a little bit comical, but Bobby was a stickler and he had started to play trumpet, as I say, only a short time previous. He was wearing tails and white tie, with his little -- let's see, a five-piece jazz band. They used no base. Every once in awhile, somebody would come charging through the club with a base over their shoulder to help out. But in that band was Brad Gowens, and I was going to do some more research on somebody else.…
